beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: You're scared of debt. I love it. Let me show you why.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: Same bank, two loans. Rohan borrows $40,000, I borrow $100,000, and one question decides who gets richer.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Mine buys a shiny new car! Just 7% a year, paid over 60 months. Easy.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: But a car loses value every year you drive it. So Rohan pays $7,523 in interest for something that keeps shrinking.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: My loan costs 6% a year. Over 10 years, that's $33,225 in interest, even more than Rohan pays.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: The difference is what I buy with it: a building, or a business that can grow.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: If it grows an assumed 8% a year, in 10 years it gains $115,892.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Hold on. You still pay the bank all that interest!

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: Gladly. The interest is my cost, the growth is my profit. Good debt buys something that earns more than the loan costs.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: That's why the rich love debt: the car shrinks, the building grows. But if what they buy stops growing, the loan still has to be paid.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: So I'm not scared of debt. I'm scared of my car loan. And honestly, Sharma...
